Prior to PIONEER-HF, guideline-directed practice typically involved stabilizing patients post-discharge for 4–6 weeks before transitioning to ARNI, resulting in significant delays in receipt of evidence-based therapy and high rates of therapy non-initiation after discharge. The trial enrolled 881 hemodynamically stabilized patients (systolic BP ≥100 mmHg, off IV diuretics for ≥6 hours) hospitalized for acute decompensated HFrEF (EF ≤40%), randomizing them to in-hospital initiation of sacubitril/valsartan (starting at 24–49mg twice daily and titrated to 97–103mg twice daily) versus enalapril (2.5–10mg twice daily). The primary endpoint of time-averaged proportional NT-proBNP reduction was significantly greater with sacubitril/valsartan (46.7% vs 25.3% reduction, ratio 0.71, p<0.001) — indicating superior reduction of cardiac wall stress and filling pressures, the pathophysiological drivers of HF decompensation. The composite of serious adverse events was reduced by 46% (8.0% vs 13.8%, HR 0.54, p=0.007). Worsening renal function and hyperkalemia rates were similar between groups. Symptomatic hypotension was more frequent with sacubitril/valsartan (15.0% vs 9.5%) — requiring careful blood pressure monitoring during initiation. PIONEER-HF directly established in-hospital ARNI initiation as a Class IIa recommendation in ACC/AHA/HFSA 2022 heart failure guidelines (GUIDE-003), enabling earlier delivery of proven therapy and improving discharge medication adherence.

full_title: Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
population: 6,263 patients with heart failure and mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (EF >40%) in NYHA Class II-IV with NT-proBNP elevation, including recently hospitalized patients
intervention: Dapagliflozin 10mg once daily added to standard therapy
primary_outcome: Composite of worsening heart failure (urgent HF visit or hospitalization) or cardiovascular death
key_results: Primary endpoint: 16.4% (dapagliflozin) vs 19.5% (placebo), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.92), p<0.001 — 18% relative reduction. Total (first + recurrent) HF events: RR 0.77 (p<0.001). CV death: 7.7% vs 8.7%, HR 0.88 (p=0.17 — not significant). Consistent benefits across EF strata including EF ≥60%. Subgroup of recently hospitalized patients derived consistent benefit.
clinical_significance: DELIVER confirmed and extended the EMPEROR-Preserved findings across a broader HFpEF population including patients with EF ≥60% (the strictest HFpEF definition) and recently hospitalized patients. Combined with EMPEROR-Preserved, DELIVER established class-level evidence for SGLT2 inhibitors as the only pharmacological therapy proven to reduce clinical events in HFpEF across its full EF spectrum. A pooled mega-analysis of DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved showed significant CV death reduction, confirming full benefit. Both dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are now Class IIa recommendations for HFpEF.
content: The DELIVER (Dapagliflozin Evaluation to Improve the LIVEs of Patients with PReserved Ejection Fraction Heart Failure) trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2022, is the confirmatory landmark trial that established the class effect of SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction, reinforcing and extending the findings of EMPEROR-Preserved with dapagliflozin across a broader and more contemporary HFpEF population. The trial enrolled 6,263 patients with symptomatic heart failure and EF above 40% — including patients with mildly reduced EF (40–49%) and those with strictly preserved EF (≥50% and ≥60%), with elevated NT-proBNP, in NYHA Class II–IV, and importantly including a significant proportion of recently hospitalized patients and those with prior EF below 40% who had recovered. The primary composite of worsening heart failure events or cardiovascular death was reduced from 19.5% to 16.4% (HR 0.82, p<0.001) — an 18% relative reduction. Total heart failure events (including recurrent events) were reduced by 23% (RR 0.77, p<0.001), demonstrating substantial prevention of repeat hospitalizations. Cardiovascular death was not significantly reduced independently (HR 0.88, p=0.17), but a subsequent pooled mega-analysis combining DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved in over 12,000 patients showed a statistically significant 14% reduction in cardiovascular death, confirming mortality benefit at the class level. Benefits were consistent across EF strata including patients with EF ≥60%, reinforcing that SGLT2 inhibitor benefit in HF extends across the full EF spectrum beyond the HFrEF-HFmrEF boundary. DELIVER, combined with EMPEROR-Preserved, provides robust class-level evidence that established both dapagliflozin and empagliflozin as Class IIa recommendations for HFpEF (EF above 40%) in ACC/AHA/HFSA 2022 heart failure guidelines (GUIDE-003) — the only pharmacological therapy with demonstrated clinical event reduction in this challenging and growing heart failure phenotype.
